sanskrit: yo no mitrāvaruṇābhidāsāt sapatno votpipāno bṛhaspate | sarvaṃ tam agne adharaṃ pātayāsmad yathendrāham uttamaś cetayāni ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, whoever rival assails us — Mitra and Varuṇa — or whatever enemy, puffed up with pride: cast him down entirely beneath us, O Agni; may I, like Indra, be perceived as the highest among them.

sanskrit: aham eṣām uttamaś cetayāni mama vaśam upa tiṣṭhantu sarve | ājuhvāno ghṛtapṛṣṭhaḥ suvarcā vasor madhye dīdihi jātavedaḥ ||
english: May I be recognized as the foremost among them; may all stand under my sway. O Jātavedas, butter-backed and radiant, blazing with oblations offered, shine in the midst of riches.

sanskrit: amum agne adharaṃ pātayāsmaj jāsayotpipānaṃ sapatnam | ye no dhūrvān adhare te bhavantu viśvā dveṣāṃsy abhito ni mṛḍḍhi ||
english: O Agni, cast that puffed-up rival down beneath us; destroy him utterly. Those who seek to harm us — let them fall lower; crush all hostilities on every side.

sanskrit: mūrdhānaṃ divo aratiṃ pṛthivyā viśas tvā sarvā balihṛta upāsatām | tāsām ugro madhyameṣṭheyam asyā sve kṣetre saviteva vi rāja ||
english: You are the head of heaven, the unwearied force of the earth; may all peoples wait upon you bearing tribute. Among them may I stand as the mighty one in their midst; rule wide in your own domain, like Savitṛ.

sanskrit: ā pratyañcaṃ dāśuṣe dāśvāṃsaṃ sarasvantaṃ puṣṭipatiṃ rayīṇām | rāyaspoṣaṃ śravasyaṃ vasānam iha huvema sadanaṃ rayīṇām ||
english: We call hither Sarasvant, who bestows upon the worshipping sacrificer, the lord of nourishment and of riches — clothed in swelling wealth and glory — the seat of riches, to come to us face to face.

sanskrit: yasya vrate paśavo yanti sarve yasya vrata upatiṣṭhanta āpaḥ | yasya vrate puṣṭipatir niviṣṭas taṃ sarasvantam avase huvema ||
english: In whose vow all cattle go; in whose vow the waters attend; in whose vow the lord of nourishment is established — that Sarasvant we call for protection.

sanskrit: ye te sarasvann ūrmayo madhumanto ghṛtaścutaḥ | tebhir no 'vitā bhuvaḥ ||
english: O Sarasvant, those waves of yours that are honey-sweet, dripping with ghee — with those be our protector.

sanskrit: divyaṃ samudraṃ payasaṃ bṛhantam apāṃ garbhaṃ vṛṣabham oṣadhīnām | abhīpato rayyā tarpayantaṃ sarasvantaṃ rayiṣṭhāṃ sādayeha ||
english: The celestial ocean, great in milky abundance, the embryo of the waters, the bull of the plants — him who satisfies the devotee with riches, Sarasvant the richest — establish here.

sanskrit: indrasya kukṣir asi somadhāna ātmā devānām uta viśvarūpaḥ | iha prajā janaya yās ta āsu yā anyatreha tās te svadhito gṛṇantu ||
english: You are the belly of Indra, the vessel of Soma, the self of the gods, and all-formed. Generate here the progeny that belongs to you; those who are elsewhere — let them here sing your praises, O self-sustaining one.

sanskrit: śyenaḥ suparṇo divyo nṛcakṣāḥ sahasrapāc chatayonir vayodhāḥ | sa no ni yacchād vasu yat parābhṛtam asmākam astu pitṛṣu svadhāvat ||
english: The divine falcon, fair-winged, man-seeing, thousand-footed, hundred-born, bestower of strength — may he bring down to us the wealth that has been carried away; let it rest with us among the fathers, rich in its own power.

sanskrit: ati dhanvāny aty apas tatarda śyeno nṛcakṣā avasānadarśaḥ | taran viśvāvarā rajāṃs- -īndreṇa sakhyā śiva ā jagāma ||
english: The falcon, man-gazing, beholding the abode, cleaved beyond the deserts and beyond the waters; crossing all the shielding regions of the air, in friendship with Indra, auspicious, he came.

sanskrit: āgan devaḥ savitā sarvadhāyā urujyotir avidāmā namobhiḥ | mahīṃ nāvam aditer ā ruhema yatra somaḥ sadam it tatra bhadram ||
english: The god Savitṛ, sustainer of all, of vast light, has come, unsubdued, with homage. May we mount the great boat of Aditi, where Soma is — there, ever, is blessing.

sanskrit: ud vayam ity ekā ||
english: [Rubric:] one [verse beginning] 'ud vayam' ('Up, we rise…').

sanskrit: patir divaḥ patir agniḥ pṛthivyāḥ patir viśvasya bhuvanasya rājati | patir viśvā oṣadhīr ā viveśa patnīvān agna iha yāhi somam ||
english: He is lord of heaven; Agni is lord of the earth; he reigns as lord of the entire world. As lord he has entered all the plants; O Agni, who has a spouse, come here to the Soma.

sanskrit: saṃ krāmataṃ mā jahītaṃ śarīraṃ prāṇāpānau sayujeha stam | saptaṛṣibhyaḥ pari dadma etaṃ ta enaṃ svasti jarase nayantu ||
english: Come together, both of you; do not abandon the body — in-breath and out-breath, be yoked here together. We entrust this one to the seven sages; may they lead him safely to old age.

sanskrit: yat ta āyur atihitaṃ parācair apānaḥ prāṇo ya u te paretaḥ | agniṣ ṭad āhār nirṛter upasthāt tad ātmani punar ā veśayāmi ||
english: Whatever life-span of yours has been set aside by those gone afar, the out-breath and the in-breath that had departed from you — Agni has retrieved them from the lap of Nirṛti; I cause them to enter back into your self.

sanskrit: mā tvā prāṇo hāsīd yas tve praviṣṭo mā tvāpāno 'vahāya parā gāt | saṃrabhya jīva śaradaḥ suvarcā agniṣ ṭe gopā adhipā vasiṣṭhaḥ ||
english: May the in-breath that has entered you not abandon you; may the out-breath not go away from you, carrying you off. Gathering strength, live your autumns in splendor; Agni, the mightiest, is your guardian and overlord.

sanskrit: rākām ahaṃ suhavāṃ suṣṭutī huve śṛṇotu naḥ subhagā bodhatu tmanā | sīvyatv apaḥ sūcyācchidyamānayā dadātu vīraṃ śatadāyam ukthyam ||
english: I invoke Rākā, easy to call, with good praise; may the bounteous one hear us, may she awaken of herself. Let her sew her work with needle and unbreaking thread; may she give a hero worthy of a hundred gifts, worthy of praise.

sanskrit: yās te rāke sumatayaḥ supeśaso yābhir dadāti dāśuṣe vasūni | tābhir no adya sumanā upāgahi sahasrapoṣaṃ subhage rarāṇā ||
english: O Rākā, those fair-formed graces of yours, by which you give treasures to the devotee — come to us today with those, well-minded, O bounteous one, bestowing a thousandfold abundance.

sanskrit: yā rākā yā sinīvālī yā guṅgūr yā sarasvatī | indrāṇīm ahva ūtaye varuṇānīṃ svastaye ||
english: Rākā, Sinīvālī, Guṅgū, Sarasvatī — I have called upon Indrāṇī for aid and Varuṇānī for well-being.

sanskrit: yā subāhuḥ svaṅguriḥ suṣumā bahusūvarī | tasyai viśpatnyai haviḥ sinīvālyai juhotana ||
english: She who has beautiful arms, fair fingers, and lovely body, rich in many beautiful forms — offer the oblation to her, the lady of the clans, Sinīvālī.

sanskrit: sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke yā devānām asi svasā | juṣasva havyam āhutaṃ prajāṃ devi didiḍḍhi naḥ ||
english: O Sinīvālī of the broad braid, you who are sister of the gods — accept the oblation poured, O goddess; grant offspring to us.

sanskrit: yā viśvata indram asi pratīcī sahasrastutām abhi yantu devīḥ | viṣṇupatni tubhyaṃ rātā havīṃṣi patiṃ devi rādhasā codayasva ||
english: You who face Indra from all sides — may the goddesses of the thousand-praised one approach. O wife of Viṣṇu, oblations are offered to you; O goddess, urge your husband on with your bounty.

sanskrit: upa hvaya iti tisraḥ ||
english: [Rubric:] three [verses beginning] 'upa hvaya' ('I call near…').

sanskrit: sūyavasād bhagavatīty ekā ||
english: [Rubric:] one [verse beginning] 'sūyavasād bhagavatī' ('The blessed one from good pasture…').

sanskrit: saṃjānānā upa sīdān abhijñu patnīvanto namasyaṃ namasyān | ririkvāṃsas tanvā sumnam āyuḥ sakhet sakhyur nimiṣi rakṣamāṇāḥ ||
english: In mutual understanding, let those who have wives sit down on bent knee, paying homage to what is worthy of homage; those who have poured out of the body, seeking well-being and life — let them be guarded in the twinkling of a friend's eye.

sanskrit: samiddho agnir aśvinā tapto vāṃ gharma ā gatam | duhyante nūnaṃ vṛṣaṇeha dhenavo dasrā vadanti kāravaḥ ||
english: The fire is kindled, O Aśvins; the hot milk-vessel is heated for you — come! The cows are being milked now, O mighty ones; the skilled singers call out, O Dasras.

sanskrit: samiddho agnir aśvinā rathī divas tapto gharmo duhyate vām iṣe madhu | vayaṃ hi vāṃ purutamāso aśvinā havāmahe sadhamādeṣu kāravaḥ ||
english: The fire is kindled, O Aśvins, O charioteers of heaven; the hot gharma is being milked for your refreshment, sweet as honey. For we, the singers, O Aśvins, invoke you most abundantly at the shared feast.

sanskrit: yad usriyāsv āhutaṃ ghṛtaṃ payo 'yaṃ so aśvinā vāṃ bhāga ā gatam | mādhvī dhartārā vidathasya satpatī taptaṃ gharmaṃ pibataṃ rocane divaḥ ||
english: The ghee and milk offered among the dawn-cows — this is your share, O Aśvins; come to it. You two sweet sustainers, true lords of the assembly, drink the heated gharma in the brilliance of heaven.

sanskrit: tapto vāṃ gharmo nakṣati suhotā pra vām adhvaryuś carati payasvān | madhor dugdhasyāśvinā tanāyā vītaṃ pātaṃ payasa usriyāyāḥ ||
english: The hot gharma hastens to you, O Aśvins, well-offered; the milk-rich adhvaryu moves forward for you. Drink your fill from the sweet milked offering, the lineage-gift — drink the milk of the dawn-cow.

sanskrit: upa drava payasā godhug oṣum ā gharme siñca paya usriyāyāḥ | vi nākam akhyat savitā vareṇyo 'nu dyāvāpṛthivī supraṇītiḥ ||
english: Run up swiftly, milkmaid, with the milk; pour the milk of the dawn-cow into the hot vessel. Savitṛ the excellent has surveyed the vault of heaven; heaven and earth follow him, well-guided.
